mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between HOUST (housing starts) and GDPC1 over the past six months indicates robust residential investment and overall demand growth, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOUST, GDPC1) > 0.7 over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST and GDPC1 are strongly correlated.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months signals accelerating employment growth, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RSAFS (retail sales) for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue for consumer-facing companies and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of strong industrial production growth.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls for 4 consecutive months and INDPRO is not rising (>0% month-over-month)
regime_hint: consumer demand weakness with flat industrial production
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls for four months and INDPRO is flat or declining.
